title: Epochal sliding-window throttle reconciler and tombstone eviction for quota continuity
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: During regional partial outages and limiter process restarts, tenant quotas drift and requests either accumulate unfairly or are shed too aggressively. This causes SLO blips for tail latency and unfair token consumption across tenants and regions.

Goal: Implement a reconciliation mechanism that preserves per-tenant fairness and SLO stability across multi-region failover and limiter outages while minimizing coordination traffic and write amplification. The design uses epochal sliding windows (short, overlapping windows with bounded state), deterministic token decomposition to split large bursts, passive snapshot propagation for warm-starts, and tombstone markers to allow graceful eviction of stale limiter state without global locks.

Why different: Rather than continuous leader-based reconciliation or heavy cross-region consensus, this approach tolerates short inconsistencies by bounding their impact in time (epoch length), using compact deltas (bounded-token-diff) for catch-up, and applying conservative admission during unknown-state windows. The net effect should reduce outage recovery time and improve fairness compared to immediate full-synchronization schemes.
acceptance_criteria: Limiter restart in a single region recovers per-tenant quotas within 2 epoch windows without exceeding per-tenant burst SLO (tail 99.9% latency)
Cross-region failover where primary region loses 30% of capacity results in <5% increase in overall token rejection for high-priority tenants compared to baseline
Observability: new reconciliation metrics emitted (epoch_gap, bounded_diff_bytes, tombstone_evictions) and dashboards created
Canary: behavior validated against synthetic traffic and one low-risk customer slice with no elevated error budget consumption during 72h canary
notes:
Design alternatives considered: 1) full RAFT across limiters (rejected due to write amplification and latency), 2) lease-based leader election for tenant shards (complex failover slow path). Chosen: epochal windows + passive snapshots because it balances throughput and bounded staleness.

Key trade-offs: slightly higher token accounting conservatism during unknown windows (more temporary rejections) vs fast recovery and reduced coordination traffic.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1: API and data model changes (epoch id in limiter state, tombstone markers), telemetry hooks.
- Phase 2: Local token decomposition routine to break incoming bursts into epoch-sized tokens and bounded diffs for replication.
- Phase 3: Passive snapshot sender on limiter exit and reconstructor on startup (use S3 for cross-region snapshots).
- Phase 4: Canary rollout with traffic-splitting and A/B verification.

Observability and alerts: New alerts for tombstone_eviction_rate > 0.1/min, epoch_gap > 2, bounded_diff_apply_failures > 5/min.

Rollout windows coordinated with SRE; approximate owner list: Ravi (eng), Priya (SRE), Maya (PM).
comments: 2026-02-17: Design review with SRE. Agreement to keep epoch length configurable per-tenant. Action: produce simulation results for epoch lengths 500ms, 2s, 5s.
2026-02-24: Simulation results uploaded. 2s epoch gives best tradeoff for our latency distribution; added to design doc.
2026-03-02: Security review kickoff. No KMS changes required; snapshots encrypted at rest in S3 already. No PII in limiter state noted.
2026-03-05: PR opened with core reconciliation and tombstone primitives (see linked PRs). Waiting on integration tests for cross-region snapshot restore.
2026-03-09: QA run: synthetic tenant mix (1000 tenants, skewed 80/20). Observed temporary +2% rejection for low-priority tenants during simulated outage; deemed acceptable by PM.
2026-03-10: Marking work In Progress after initial unit + integration tests pass. Planning canary for 2026-03-18.
testing_plan: Unit tests for epoch math and bounded diff generation
Integration tests: limiter restart across S3 snapshot restore (single region, cross-region)
Chaos test: kill 20% limiter processes mid-burst and measure fairness and SLO compliance
Canary: route 1% of traffic for 72h and monitor errors/latency/cost
rollback_plan: Feature flags for epochal reconciliation are behind a runtime flag per-deployment. Canary can be disabled to revert to existing limiter behavior. If snapshot restore causes systemic errors, disable cross-region snapshot apply and fallback to conservative conservative-local-only mode, then investigate logs and bounded_diff_apply_failures metric.
